steps.message:
# Focus ends up in the wrong place

Two scenarios, A and B, are captured frame by frame in the attached images. Each caption states the action performed, and the ring marks where keyboard focus is afterwards.

In each scenario the last frame (A4 and B3) shows a wrong result. The matching "Expected" image shows where focus should go instead.

## Expected

Make both scenarios behave as in the Expected images. Each Expected image shows one acceptable outcome; what matters is where focus goes relative to the buttons on the page.

Keep all other behavior unchanged, including the earlier frames and whatever the same keys do afterwards.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/screen.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/focus_trace_1.png` … `focus_trace_4.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/expected_A.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/disabled_trace_1.png` … `disabled_trace_3.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/expected_B.png`

Inspect every attached file before making changes. The images describe observable behavior; they do not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

I couldn't look at any of the screenshots: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and none of the images exist anywhere on the machine. So I had to infer the two scenarios from the code. I fixed the bugs that best fit your descriptions, but **I can't confirm they're the ones in your images.** If you can re-attach the images, I'll check against them.

**What I found.** I simulated keyboard Tab on a plain page of buttons. Tab picked the wrong button in these cases, compared with what a browser does:

1. **A focused button becomes disabled, hidden or inert, then you press Tab.** Focus stayed stuck on that button. A browser moves on to the next button (or the previous one with Shift+Tab). This is my best guess for scenario B.
2. **A focused button is removed from the page, then you press Tab.** Focus jumped back to the first button. A browser carries on from where the removed button was. This might be scenario A, since the earlier steps look normal and only the last Tab goes wrong.
3. **A `disabled` button that also has a `tabindex`** still received focus. Browsers never focus disabled controls.

**What I changed**
- `packages/ariakit-core/src/utils/focus.ts`:
  - Disabled form controls no longer count as focusable, even with a `tabindex`.
  - Finding the next or previous tabbable element now works from the active element's position on the page when that element is no longer focusable.
- `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`:
  - Tab still works when the focused element has just become unfocusable.
  - When the focused element is removed, the next Tab continues from where it was. This only applies when its parent is still on the page. If the whole tree is unmounted, as happens between tests, Tab starts over from the top of the page as before.
- `packages/ariakit-test/src/__tests__/press-tab-test.ts`: 6 new tests. All 6 fail on the original code and pass now.

**Checks:** the full suite passes (616 existing tests plus the 6 new ones), and type-checking and lint are clean.

**Approach I dropped:** I also tried making Tab move focus off the page after the last button, as a browser does. It broke 6 existing dialog tests, which expect focus to stay put at the end, so I reverted it. If your scenario A is actually "Tab past the last button", it isn't covered.
